title: Nuclear Dissociation of Adult C. elegans for Single-Nucleus RNA Sequencing
author: Levenson, Barrere-Cain, et al.

steps.title: Prepare OP50 + M9 stock
steps.instruction: Generate a 100 mg/mL OP50 bacterial suspension in M9 buffer for downstream nuclei isolation.

substeps.instruction: Pick a single OP50 colony into a sterile 1 L Erlenmeyer flask containing 100 mL Luria Broth; incubate overnight with shaking at 37 °C.
Transfer the overnight culture evenly into three sterile, pre‑weighed 50 mL centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes at 4000 × g for 5 min; carefully remove and discard the supernatant.
Re‑weigh each tube to determine the mass of the bacterial pellet.
Resuspend each pellet in M9 buffer (stored at room temperature, stable up to 1 year) to achieve a final concentration of 100 mg/mL OP50 + M9.

steps.title: Prepare nuclei dissociation reagents
steps.instruction: Assemble all reagents needed for the nuclei dissociation step on the day of the experiment.

substeps.instruction: Dilute DAPI (or Hoechst) stain from a 2.5 mg/mL stock (stored at 4 °C, stable up to 1 month) to the working concentration needed for staining.
Prepare Modified FA buffer as described by Jonge et al., 2020; store at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks and add protease and RNase inhibitors fresh before use.
Make RNase‑free 1× PBS by diluting commercial 10× PBS with DEPC‑treated water (see key resources) to a final volume of 2 mL per condition.
Prepare 1 mL of RNase‑free water containing protease‑inhibitor tablet(s) according to the manufacturer’s instructions; keep on ice and use the same day.

description: The identification of cell-specific responses to environmental factors has long been unattainable using conventional bulk RNA-sequencing. By contrast, single-cell RNA sequencing has enabled a deeper examination of tissue and cellular heterogeneity under normal conditions or under stress, including environmental stress.2,3 Single cell approaches have been applied to the model organism Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans) to comprehensively capture the transcriptome of individual cells but at the scale of a whole organism.4,5,6 However, up to 30% of all somatic cells in the nematode are multinucleated while the adult germline is also primarily syncytial.7,8 Thus, single cell techniques are not able to capture the complexity of such organs, tissues, and cell types or their response to environmental cues. We recently published the development and application of a single nucleus dissociation followed by single nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) at the scale of the entire adult C. elegans.1 This approach was not only used to capture the transcriptome of all major cell types in the nematode but also to identify the heterogeneity in cell-specific responses to ethanol across generations. The protocol presented here covers the key aspects of the methodology, including the exposure protocol that was followed as well as the isolation of high-quality nuclei from the adult C. elegans.
